scope: Repository source audit and committed-archive measurements from GitHub Actions. GMGN live backfill has not been run.

changes: Cursor pagination supports activities/list/data response shapes, including nested cursors and multiline JSON output.
Checkpoint/resume persists each successful page; a completed archive is merged with prior records and replaced only after completeness checks.
Malformed responses, command failures, repeated cursors, and full pages without a cursor are marked failed_or_incomplete; prior completed archives are left untouched.
API-key preflight prevents unauthenticated requests; page limit is validated; the run is capped at 1000 pages with resumable checkpoints.
Wallet-specific backfill can target one explicit chain; Solana wallet/token identity preserves base58 case while EVM identity is normalized.
JSON writes are atomic and timestamp sorting accepts numeric, millisecond, and ISO timestamps.
Rows fetched from each chain are tagged with that requested chain if the provider omits chain metadata.
Live portfolio/activity reads now follow cursor pages with a three-page per-wallet cap and count every page against the existing 300-call budget.
An incomplete live cursor window is discarded and falls back to stored history rather than being treated as complete evidence.
GMGN rows are tagged with the requested chain before signals/history are built.
History deduplication includes price so two same-second events at different prices are not silently collapsed.
A baseline snapshot is taken before a run; before compression, every distinct prior event identity must still exist in the new history.
Exact duplicate compaction is allowed, but missing unique events, malformed JSON, invalid history shape, or a destructive rebase conflict fail closed without replacing the remote archive.
Removed git rebase -X theirs from the main scanner and GMGN smart-money writers; conflicts no longer prefer a potentially stale local archive.
The raw history is JSON-validated before compression and the compressed archive is validated before commit.
Completed schema-v2 GMGN portfolio/activity archives are normalized into historical discovery with chain+contract identity and per-file hashes.
Partial checkpoints, status files, old placeholder artifacts, and Nansen balance snapshots are excluded.
Rows with no known chain are excluded from cross-chain asset observations, preventing a bare contract address from being incorrectly treated as a chain+contract identity.
Fixed JSON newline escaping so checkpoints and archives remain parseable.

Added offline tests for pagination, resume/merge safety, chain attribution, case sensitivity, incomplete live windows, baseline preservation, compressed archive validity, and supplemental discovery ingestion.
Pull-request CI runs the new tests and a read-only inventory of the committed compressed archive.
The scanner workflow now regenerates and commits reverse_historical_discovery.json from the updated archive, including completed supplemental GMGN activity archives.

The discovery script reads either raw JSON or the committed gzip archive, records the decompressed payload checksum, and keeps generated_at stable when evidence is unchanged to avoid unnecessary commits.

previous_audit_snapshot.note: These are the committed audit's measured values for the historical snapshot, not a fresh provider query.

not_yet_verified_or_not_yet_solved: No live GMGN backfill has been run. The secret value is not inspectable here, and actual GMGN cursor responses, quota, and available historical depth remain unverified.
The manual backfill handles one wallet and one selected chain per run; automatic enumeration and batch backfill of the full discovered-wallet population is not implemented.

The current archive spans about 24.75 days overall, and the longest observed history for a known-chain contract is about 17.9 days. No asset has 90/180/365 days, so the existing archive cannot satisfy the 90-day discovery gate.

123,184 existing rows have no usable chain attribution and the rows contain no alternative network/chain-id field. Their chain cannot be inferred safely from the current archive; they are retained but excluded from cross-chain historical discovery. New scanner and GMGN-layer rows now inherit the requested chain.
The legacy historical-depth audit's source digest does not match the current compressed archive; the legacy report is a prior snapshot, not a current measurement.
Nansen historical-balance backfill stopped after 1,000 rows because the provider returned HTTP 403 insufficient_credits; balance snapshots are not substitute trade history.
The code and offline tests are repaired, but historical coverage cannot be declared complete until a successful live GMGN backfill provides and verifies older trade events.

safety.note: No live-order setting was enabled or changed.

observed_provider_run.interpretation: This verifies some Nansen historical-balance access, but credits ran out. These are balance snapshots, not trade events, and they are excluded from trade reconstruction.

current_archive_audit.note: This is a measured snapshot; scheduled runs may append new rows after it.
